VARZIN — Publications & Archive Registry

Research records, corrections, access history, and archival provenance

Registry scope: This page records the publication and archive history currently maintained by the VARZIN Project. It distinguishes active research records from corrected versions, access-history records, and records removed from public access by the author. Platform-specific archival status is not generalized here.

Current research records

Nirouyar, R. (2026). VARZIN Level-1 Computational Stack: Finite Affine Core, Genomic Scanner, and Torus Manifold Solver (Version v2.0.0) [Computer software]. Zenodo. 10.5281/zenodo.22036769

Nirouyar, R. (2026). Morphemes vs. Manifolds: Diagnosing Structural Blindness and Morphological Hijacking in Large Language Models via Finite Affine Orbits (Version v1.0.0). Zenodo. 10.5281/zenodo.22101179

Nirouyar, R. (2026). LUXVAR: A Constructed Language with Distinctive Morphemic Structure and AI-Recoverable Morpheme Families (historical title) (historically listed as Version v2.2; deposit-version identity partly unresolved). Zenodo. 10.5281/zenodo.22115483

OSF record: 10.17605/OSF.IO/YEGJ8

Scientific-status note: the historical title of the LUXVAR v2.2 record retains the phrase “AI-Recoverable” for citation continuity. The project’s later audit interpretation does not treat independent AI recovery as an established result.

Version and access history: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20691858 and 10.5281/zenodo.22115483 are retained as separate DOI identities. Project materials associate 20691858 with v2.1, but a local file named v2.2 contains an internal v2.1 identity, and the corresponding deposited artifact for 22115483 was not independently identified in the audited set. Their exact version mapping remains partially unresolved.

The “Withdrawal requested” row labels reproduce the historical project action register. Following the project’s adversarial audit, the author subsequently removed the 29 earlier records from public access. This table does not certify their present platform-specific archival status. HOLD: 2NKZA appears in this old register, while later project documentation identifies it as a VPE-001A registration. Its identity and current access status require primary platform reconciliation.
